author: reek
body: The cursor primitives (save-under patch, restore, draw) live in GopDraw so the desktop shell shares them. A pointer position maps to the menu row whose selection bar covers it, or to no row at all.

author: reek
body: One pure step handles everything short of leaving the loop: keyboard first (a queued scancode must never be lost to a mouse twitch), then the pointer -- a click confirms the hovered row, plain hover moves the bar. Any repaint invalidates the cursor patch; a movement repaints the cursor last, so it rides above whatever was drawn.

author: reek
body: The desktop borrows the whole panel; when it returns (Esc or its close box) the menu redraws and the cursor patch is invalidated -- the desktop's cursor state block is its own.

author: reek
body: Read LBA 1 of the boot disk with the payload's own drivers (AHCI first, then legacy IDE PIO) and check for the GPT header signature "EFI PART". Firmware is gone, so a hit proves the running program reached its own boot medium unaided. The screen names the controller that answered.

author: reek
body: Mount the stick's own EFI System Partition and resolve the loader that the firmware booted a moment ago -- the payload finding, through its own drivers and its own filesystem code, the very file it was launched from.

author: reek
body: Read the seed itself off the stick -- 2.1 MB through the payload's own driver, filesystem, and FAT chain -- and check the CDX magic in the header it just fetched. This is the compiler that compiled this program, recovered from the medium it booted from. Verifying its signature is B3.4 (WakeCeremony).

author: reek
body: The first act of a machine that cannot ask anyone what it is. It reads its own seed off its own stick, recomputes the hash over those bytes, checks the author signature, and speaks only what it checked -- or says it does not verify and refuses to act. Ascent V, rung 3.

author: reek
body: The report is computed before anything is drawn: the screen reports a verdict, it does not narrate a hope.

author: reek
body: H3c: the machine names every disk it can reach -- controller, model from the device's own identify data, size, ESP volume label, and whether our CODEX.CDX is aboard -- and points at the one it booted from. The enumeration walks GopEnum's candidates and restores the medium lock, so the line marked as the boot medium is read from the same cells every later storage call obeys.

author: reek
body: The first act on the boot path is runtime-init (H1a): GDT, IDT, TSS, syscall MSRs, then the PIC/PIT/keyboard setup ending in sti -- which also re-enables the PS/2 keyboard interface and scanning that firmware often leaves disabled after ExitBootServices (and skips itself cleanly on a machine with no i8042 at all). From here ticks run, keystrokes arrive by IRQ, and a fault dumps !EXC instead of triple faulting. Second act: usb-attach (H2) enumerates the USB bus ONCE -- keyboard and boot-stick disk configured on the same running controller, the disk handle published so every later storage call transfers without a reset. On a machine with no PS/2 controller the USB keyboard is the only input there is; a machine without one gets kbd-no-kbd, whose pump is a flag test. Third act: medium-select probes every disk for our own CODEX.CDX and locks GopDisk onto the one carrying it, so a real machine's internal drive cannot shadow the boot stick. The first-boot ceremony (GopWizard) runs next, then the interface menu takes over.

author: reek
body: On real metal there is no serial log, so the boot narrates itself on the glass. Before the runtime spine comes up -- when the only working thing is the framebuffer the stub handed over -- four bright bars and the mode numbers are painted with the REPORTED stride: a stride or mode mismatch shows as banded smear instead of clean bars, and the bar ORDER (red, green, blue, white) exposes a BGR/RGB pixel-format swap at a glance. After each boot stage a green trace line lands top-right; on a machine that hangs, the last line standing names the stage that died. A healthy boot shows the diag for a couple of seconds and the wizard then paints over all of it -- the diag matters exactly on the machine that never gets that far.

author: reek
body: The trace column lives in the diag's black bottom region so paint damage at the top of the panel cannot eat it. Every stage writes a line when it STARTS and another when it completes: on a machine that dies mid-stage, the last line names the stage that died.
